name: Persian Rose
lede: Persian Rose is a vivid magenta pink, the most saturated member of a small family of color names built on Persia, first recorded in 1922.

sections.title: A vivid member of the family
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary records Persian Rose from 1922, on plate 50, swatch K7 [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 files it as a vivid reddish purple, but the fit is loose, 9.0 units from that block's center, our swatch sitting toward the saturated edge of the block rather than its middle [1]. Our library gives it the Munsell notation 4.7RP 5.7/19.4[1].

Its nearest named neighbors are Deep Pink, 2.8 units away, then Barbie Pink at 3.0 [1]. It shares its first word with [[persian-pink]], [[persian-plum]] and [[persian-orange]], a small family that spans pink, red and orange without a documented reason for any one of them [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Like its family member [[persian-pink]], Persian Rose's hue does not come within six units of any area color in our archive of 23,781 paintings, so it has no measurable presence there [2]. Both are far more saturated than oil paint pigments typically reach, which is why neither turns up as a dominant canvas color even once [2]. That absence is itself a kind of field note: the most vivid names in a color dictionary are often the ones photographs of old paintings never confirm [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].

origin.named_after: Persia (now Iran); the specific reason for this pink is undocumented
